panels.title: Host status

targets.expr: label_replace(label_replace(up{job=~".+-node", instance=~".+:9121", always_on="true"} or (2 * up{job=~".+-node", instance=~".+:9121", always_on="false"} - 1), "host", "$1", "instance", "([^:]+)(:.*)?"), "host", "de-msa2", "host", "127\\.0\\.0\\.1|localhost")

panels.description: node-exporter scrape. Intermittent hosts (always_on="false": laptops, desktops) show OFF instead of DOWN, as they are powered off on purpose.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since boot. A short uptime on an always-on host means it rebooted unexpectedly.

panels.title: Failed systemd units
panels.description: Units in the `failed` state right now (same source as the SystemdUnitFailed alert). Empty = healthy.

panels.title: Power draw
panels.description: Real power drawn from the UPS output: ups.load (% of the 3000 VA rating) x 3000 VA x output.powerfactor. The UPS reports no ups.realpower, and load has 1 % resolution, so the value moves in steps of ~27 W. Thresholds: yellow at 50 %, red at 80 % of the 2700 W real-power limit.

panels.title: UPS status
panels.description: Most severe flag of ups.status. ON BATTERY means mains failed; LOW BATTERY means upsmon starts the shutdown. UNKNOWN: no flag set; No data: the exporter or driver is down.

targets.expr:
max(
  network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="OL"} * 1
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="TRIM"} * 2
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="BOOST"} * 2
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="RB"} * 3
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="BYPASS"} * 4
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="OB"} * 5
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="LB"} * 6
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="OVER"} * 7
  or network_ups_tools_ups_status{flag="FSD"} * 8
)

panels.title: Load
panels.description: ups.load: share of the 3000 VA rating in use. Above 100 % the UPS goes to bypass or shuts off.

panels.title: Battery runtime
panels.description: battery.runtime: the UPS's own estimate of time on battery at the current load. It falls when load rises.

panels.title: Energy (last 24h)
panels.description: Mean power draw over the last 24 h x 24 h. Covers everything plugged into the UPS.

panels.title: Power draw (dashed = UPS real-power limit)
panels.description: Same formula as the 'Power draw' stat. The dashed line is 3000 VA x power factor, the most the UPS can deliver.

panels.title: Mains & output voltage
panels.description: input.voltage is the mains side; the UPS is online (double conversion), so output.voltage stays at 230 V while input moves. It switches to battery outside input.transfer.low/high (218 / 242 V).

panels.title: Battery voltage & UPS temperature
panels.description: Battery voltage drops while discharging (nominal 72 V, low cutoff 62.4 V). A steady rise in UPS temperature shortens battery life.

panels.title: Load average 1m
panels.description: node_load1 per host. See 'Load per core' for values normalized by thread count.

panels.title: Load average 5m
panels.description: node_load5 per host. See 'Load per core' for values normalized by thread count.

panels.title: Load average 15m
panels.description: node_load15 per host. See 'Load per core' for values normalized by thread count.

panels.title: Load per core (1m dotted / 5m / 15m bold)
panels.description: Load average divided by logical CPU count. 100% = as many runnable tasks as hardware threads.

panels.title: Available memory
panels.description: MemAvailable: free + reclaimable page cache. MemFree alone understates usable memory.

panels.title: Filesystem free (non-ZFS)
panels.description: All real block-device mounts; /nix/store is a bind mount of / and is skipped. ZFS datasets are in the ZFS row.

panels.title: Disk read
panels.description: Per whole disk (partitions, zvols and dm devices excluded).

panels.title: Disk write
panels.description: Per whole disk (partitions, zvols and dm devices excluded).

panels.title: Disk busy
panels.description: Fraction of time the disk had I/O in flight. Near 100% on an HDD = saturated; NVMe can serve many parallel requests, so this is a weaker signal there.

panels.title: CPU pressure (some)
panels.description: Linux PSI. Share of wall time in which runnable tasks waited for a CPU. The kernel does not report a meaningful system-wide "full" for CPU.

panels.title: Memory pressure (some / full bold)
panels.description: Linux PSI. Share of wall time in which some (thin) / all (bold) non-idle tasks were stalled. Unlike load average, this measures lost time directly.

panels.title: IO pressure (some / full bold)
panels.description: Linux PSI. Share of wall time in which some (thin) / all (bold) non-idle tasks were stalled. Unlike load average, this measures lost time directly.

panels.title: Errors (tx dashed)
panels.description: Physical NICs only (same filter as Receive/Transmit). Should be flat zero; tx is dashed.

panels.title: Drops (tx dashed)
panels.description: Physical NICs only (same filter as Receive/Transmit). Should be flat zero; tx is dashed.

panels.title: CPU temperature (hottest sensor)
panels.description: Max over all CPU package/CCD sensors (k10temp Tctl/Tccd*, coretemp) per host. AMD Tctl throttles at ~95 C.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: NVIDIA dGPUs via nvidia-gpu exporter, AMD iGPUs via hwmon "edge" sensor.

targets.expr: label_replace(label_replace(max by (instance, chip) (node_hwmon_temp_celsius * on (instance, chip) group_left (chip_name) node_hwmon_chip_names{chip_name=~"amdgpu"}), "host", "$1", "instance", "([^:]+)(:.*)?"), "host", "de-msa2", "host", "127\\.0\\.0\\.1|localhost")

panels.title: NVMe temperature (composite)
panels.description: NVMe "Composite" sensor per drive. Most drives start thermal throttling at ~70-80 C.

panels.title: DIMM temperature
panels.description: DDR5 SPD hub sensors (spd5118), one series per DIMM.

panels.title: SMART overall health
panels.description: smartctl self-assessment per disk. FAILED means the drive itself predicts failure: replace it.

panels.title: NVMe wear (percentage used)
panels.description: Vendor estimate of rated endurance used. Can go above 100%; the drive keeps working but is out of warranty.

panels.title: NVMe available spare
panels.description: Remaining spare blocks. The drive raises a critical warning when this drops below the vendor threshold (usually 10%).

panels.title: Error counters (any > 0 is bad)
panels.description: NVMe: media errors and the critical_warning bitfield. SATA: reallocated, pending and offline-uncorrectable sector counts (raw).
